ants.description: ANTs extracts information from complex datasets that include imaging. Paired with ANTsR, ANTs is useful for managing, interpreting and visualizing multidimensional data. ANTs is popularly considered a state-of-the-art medical image registration and segmentation toolkit. ANTsR is an emerging tool supporting standardized multimodality image analysis. ANTs depends on the Insight ToolKit (ITK), a widely used medical image processing library to which ANTs developers contribute. A summary of some ANTs findings and tutorial material (most of which is on this page) is here.\

elastix.description: a toolbox for rigid and nonrigid registration of images. elastix is open source software, based on the well-known Insight Segmentation and Registration Toolkit (ITK). The software consists of a collection of algorithms that are commonly used to perform (medical) image registration: the task of finding a spatial transformation, mapping one image (the fixed image) to another (the moving image), by optimizing relevant image similarity metrics. The modular design of elastix allows the user to quickly configure, test, and compare different registration methods for a specific application. A command-line interface enables automated processing of large numbers of data sets, by means of scripting. Nowadays elastix is accompanied by ITKElastix making it available in Python (on Pypi) and by SimpleElastix, making it available in languages like C++, Python, Java, R, Ruby, C# and Lua.
elastix.citation:
S. Klein, M. Staring, K. Murphy, M.A. Viergever, J.P.W. Pluim, "elastix: a toolbox for intensity based medical image registration," IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging, vol. 29, no. 1, pp. 196 - 205, January 2010.

This popularity suggests that it fulfills an important niche. While scientists are often encouraged to discover novel solutions, it sometimes seems that replication is undervalued. petfit.description: PETFit is a BIDS App and R Shiny application suite built on kinfitr for reproducible Positron Emission Tomography (PET) pharmacokinetic modeling. It provides interactive web apps and non-interactive automatic pipelines for combining regional time-activity curves (regiondef), plasma-input compartmental and graphical modeling (1TCM, 2TCM, 2TCM_irr, Logan, MA1, Patlak), and reference-tissue modeling (SRTM, SRTM2, SUV/SUVR, refLogan, MRTM1, MRTM2, refPatlak), generating HTML quality-control reports for each processing step.

petprep.description: PETPrep is a positron emission tomography (PET) data preprocessing pipeline that is designed to provide an easily accessible, state-of-the-art interface that is robust to variations in scan acquisition protocols and that requires minimal user input, while providing easily interpretable and comprehensive error and output reporting. It performs comprehensive processing steps—such as motion correction, segmentation, registration, partial volume correction, and extraction of time activity curves, providing outputs that can be easily submitted to a variety of group level analyses, pharmacokinetic modelling, graph theory measures, and surface or volume-based statistics.

quantiphyse.description: Quantiphyse is a volumetric medical-image viewer and analysis application. This recipe includes its ASL and Fabber plugins, OXASL Python extensions, and a minimal FSL backend with ASL models, image utilities, BET and FLIRT. Start the graphical application with quantiphyse. A display is required. Use quantiphyse-python for Python scripts in the same environment. Headless batch scripts run with quantiphyse --batch /path/to/script.yaml. Quantiphyse: 0.9.10 ASL plugin: 0.9.3.post4 Fabber plugin: 0.9.2 The smoke test checks plugin discovery, label/control subtraction, a small ASL model fit and the GUI's ASL controls under Xvfb. These checks do not validate clinical accuracy. This is not a complete FSL installation: standard space templates, FAST, FNIRT and MCFLIRT are not bundled. OXASL workflows that require those tools need a full FSL environment and separate validation. The minimal backend uses an explicit artifact/checksum lock. Refresh the whole lock together when changing backend versions, then repeat model and GUI tests. Dependency source checks verify the pinned FSL artifacts. OXASL_ENABLE is not included: its Oxford academic licence forbids redistribution, and oxasl treats it as optional. oxasl_mp is built from the Apache-2.0 upstream commit because the only PyPI release (2.0.1) predates the relicensing and lacks the run() entrypoint that oxasl 0.2.3 calls. The bundled pyfab 0.3.6 has a Python 3.10 compatibility patch that moves Sequence lookups to collections.abc. The smoke test exercises the model parameter-evaluation path that requires it. Quantiphyse and its plugins are Apache-2.0. FSL components have separate terms, including restrictions on commercial use. See the upstream licenses and /opt/licenses/quantiphyse before use or redistribution. Upstream: https://quantiphyse.readthedocs.io/en/latest/asl/asl.html

root.description: ROOT is a powerful software framework, an open source project coordinated by the European Organisation for Nuclear Research, CERN in Geneva. ROOT is very flexible and provides both a programming interface to use in own applications and a graphical user interface for interactive data analysis. ROOT leads a double life. It has an interpreter for macros (Cling) that you can run from the command line or run like applications. But it is also an interactive shell that can evaluate arbitrary statements and expressions. This is extremely useful for debugging, quick hacking and testing. Let us first have a look at some very simple examples. start the root shell with the command 'root', try things like 'TMath::Pi()' or plotting a function
root.citation: Brun R, Rademakers F. ROOT — An object oriented data analysis framework. Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A. 1997;389(1-2):81-86. doi:10.1016/S0168-9002(97)00048-X

rstudio.description: RStudio is an integrated development environment (IDE) for R. It includes a console, syntax-highlighting editor that supports direct code execution, as well as tools for plotting, history, debugging and workspace management. This container includes both RStudio Desktop (GUI) and RStudio Server (web-based).

slicer.description: 3D Slicer is a software application for visualization and analysis of medical image computing data sets. Supports images, segmentations, surfaces, annotations, transformations in 2D, 3D, and 4D.
slicer.citation: Fedorov A, Beichel R, Kalpathy-Cramer J, et al. 3D Slicer as an image computing platform for the Quantitative Imaging Network. Magn Reson Imaging. 2012;30(9):1323-1341. doi:10.1016/j.mri.2012.05.001

spm12.description: SPM12 standalone with Matlab Compiler Runtime included

spm12bi.description: SPM12 standalone with Matlab Compiler Runtime

spm25.description:
Statistical Parametric Mapping refers to the construction and assessment of spatially extended statistical processes used to test hypotheses about functional imaging data. These ideas have been instantiated in a free and open source software that is called SPM.

The SPM software package has been designed for the analysis of brain imaging data sequences. The sequences can be a series of images from different cohorts, or time-series from the same subject. The current release is designed for the analysis of fMRI, PET, SPECT, EEG and MEG.
spm25.citation: Tierney, Tim M., Nicholas A. Alexander, John Ashburner, et al. “SPM 25: Open Source Neuroimaging Analysis Software.” Journal of Open Source Software 10, no. 110 (2025): 8103. https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.08103.

stir.description: Software for Tomographic Image Reconstruction provides CPU PET and SPECT reconstruction, including `OSMAPOSL`, `FBP2D`, `FBP3DRP`, and `generate_image`. This build uses the stable STIR 6.5.0 source release. Python bindings, ITK, ROOT, CUDA, NiftyPET, and parallelproj support are disabled. Interfile support and STIR's CPU ray-tracing projectors are included. The release's Python bindings are incompatible with Debian's SWIG 4.1; this container provides the reconstruction command-line utilities. To run the bundled reconstruction example in a writable directory:
stir.citation: Thielemans K, Tsoumpas C, Mustafovic S, et al. STIR: software for tomographic image reconstruction release 2. Phys Med Biol. 2012;57(4):867-883. doi:10.1088/0031-9155/57/4/867

totalsegmentator.description: Tool for segmentation of most major anatomical structures in any CT or MR image. It was trained on a wide range of different CT and MR images (different scanners, institutions, protocols,...) and therefore works well on most images. A large part of the training dataset can be downloaded here: CT dataset (1228 subjects) and MR dataset (616 subjects). You can also try the tool online at totalsegmentator.com or as 3D Slicer extension.
totalsegmentator.citation: Wasserthal, J., Breit, H.-C., Meyer, M.T., Pradella, M., Hinck, D., Sauter, A.W., Heye, T., Boll, D., Cyriac, J., Yang, S., Bach, M., Segeroth, M., 2023. TotalSegmentator: Robust Segmentation of 104 Anatomic Structures in CT Images. Radiology: Artificial Intelligence. https://doi.org/10.1148/ryai.230024

tpcclib.citation: Oikonen V, Johansson J, Liukko K, Merisaari H, Alenius S, Laakkonen C, Krais R. TPCCLIB: Turku PET Centre C library and command-line tools for processing and analysing PET data. https://gitlab.utu.fi/vesoik/tpcclib

vesselvio.description: VesselVio is an open-source application designed to allow researchers to analyze and visualize segmented vasculature datasets.

vmtk.description: The Vascular Modeling Toolkit is a collection of libraries and tools for 3D reconstruction, geometric analysis, mesh generation, and surface data analysis for image-based modeling of blood vessels. VMTK can be used through its command line tools, as Python/C++ libraries, or as part of 3D Slicer workflows. This container builds upstream VMTK 1.5.2 from source with its individual command launchers and TetGen support. The locked conda-forge development environment supplies VTK 9.6.2, ITK 5.4.5, and Python 3.12.15. Homepage: http://www.vmtk.org/ Documentation: http://www.vmtk.org/documentation/
vmtk.citation: Izzo R, Steinman D, Manini S, Antiga L. The Vascular Modeling Toolkit: A Python Library for the Analysis of Tubular Structures in Medical Images. J Open Source Softw. 2018;3(25):745. doi:10.21105/joss.00745

voreen.description: Voreen is an open source rapid application development framework for the interactive visualization and analysis of multi-modal volumetric data sets. It provides GPU-based volume rendering and data analysis techniques.
voreen.citation:
Jennis Meyer-Spradow, Timo Ropinski, Jorg Mensmann, Klaus H. Hinrichs:
Voreen: A Rapid-Prototyping Environment for Ray-Casting-Based Volume Visualizations. IEEE Computer Graphics and Applications 29(6): 6-13 (2009)

xnat.description: XNAT 1.10.0 with native PostgreSQL, Tomcat and Java on both architectures. Start the deployed xnat command from a writable working directory as an ordinary user. Runtime state is written below xnat-runtime in that directory. Initial setup uses the normal XNAT setup UI/API; configure the site and credentials before regular use. Runtime tests start the real server, initialize the database and site, create a project through the authenticated API and verify a complete NIfTI upload/download with access checks.
xnat.citation: Marcus DS, Olsen TR, Ramaratnam M, Buckner RL. The extensible neuroimaging archive toolkit: an informatics platform for managing, exploring, and sharing neuroimaging data. Neuroinformatics. 2007;5(1):11-33. doi:10.1385/NI:5:1:11
